name: Mafea
sweep_summary: Mafea/Mavea (mafe1237) is not in the catalog. The sole sweep item (Glottolog 524313, Zawaydeh et al. 2002 on Arabic rhythm) is a false Glottolog language tag - the reference record itself says 'computerized assignment from discovering' - and is irrelevant. The best first-hand stress statement is already on file and was re-read: Guérin & Aoyama 2009 (JIPA Illustration, p. 258): predominantly penultimate primary stress, non-phonemic, secondary stress on alternate syllables leftward, with two hedged exceptions (closed-final lexemes analysed as underlyingly penultimate; final stress on some disyllabic verbs in serial constructions); length non-phonemic. Copy Guérin 2011 A Grammar of Mavea (UHP/De Gruyter) has a section 2.3 'Word Stress' (p. 28) with 2.3.1 'Exceptions to penultimate stress' (p. 29) per the open JCU front-matter PDF (saved), but the body is paywalled (doi:10.1515/9780824837068-003); medium priority to acquire for the fuller statement. Semantic Scholar API rate-limited; Crossref, UH ScholarSpace and archive.org queries yielded no further open sources. If Mafea were added to the catalog it would code as penultimate (quantity-insensitive, with secondary alternation), citing Guérin & Aoyama 2009 p. 258.

new_statements.quote: Primary stress falls predominantly on the penultimate syllable. Adding a suffix shifts the stress, suggesting that stress is not phonemic. ... Secondary stress falls on every second syllable to the left of the syllable receiving primary stress. ... We found at least two exceptions to the claim that stress is on the penult in Mavea. (i) There are some lexemes whose last syllable is closed, and which are clearly stressed on that last syllable. ... (ii) Stress sometimes falls on the last (open) syllable of a disyllabic verb.
new_statements.citation: Guérin, Valérie & Katsura Aoyama. 2009. Mavea (Illustrations of the IPA). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 39(2): 249-262. doi:10.1017/S0025100309003958
new_statements.locator: p. 258, sections 'Stress' and 'Exceptions to penultimate stress placement' (exception (ii) continues on p. 259; fn. 14 on p. 258; vowel length statement p. 256)
new_statements.reading: Mavea word stress is quantity-insensitive penultimate primary stress (non-phonemic, moves with suffixation), with secondary stress on alternate syllables leftward from the primary (e.g. [ˌpatuˈiːra] 'their head', [taˌmanaˈtːuːku] 'my husband'). The describers treat the closed-final-syllable cases (e.g. [taˈmʷam] 'your father') as penultimate at an underlying level via a lost possessive vowel, and record but do not adopt a reviewer's weight-based reading (closed final syllable always stressed, fn. 14); final stress on some disyllabic verbs is attributed to serial-verb-construction phrasing and flagged as needing validation. Length is not phonemic; stressed vowels lengthen (p. 256). First-hand (first author's own fieldwork 2005-2007), same describer as the 2011 UHP reference grammar whose TOC (open JCU copy) confirms the 'penultimate stress with exceptions' analysis.
